Hi Rajiv —

Thanks for the clear list. High level guidance below — I attached a 1-page matrix and a sample PO you can share with your AP team.

Short answer: Private Offer is typically the smoother route for sellers who must appear as bill-to on invoices and for customers that require a single PO / single-SKU mapping. Public Marketplace listing works well when a buyer wants self-serve provisioning and shorter procurement cycle, but it can complicate seller-of-record and PO handling depending on the cloud marketplace (AWS/Azure/GCP).

Key tradeoffs (concise):
- Seller-of-record / invoicing:
  - Marketplace (public): Seller-of-record may be the marketplace (platform) or a reseller depending on listing type; invoices often come from the marketplace and can show multiple line items (bad for single-SKU AP systems).
  - Private Offer: Seller provides invoice (or marketplace routes to seller per private offer flow). Easier to get seller as bill-to and to accept a PO directly.

- PO and SKU constraints:
  - Marketplace public listing: SKU granularity can be multi-line; some marketplaces allow custom SKU mapping but it's slower and varies by cloud.
  - Private Offer: We can create a single, customer-specific SKU or SKU mapping so your AP only sees one line.

- Co-sell / channel credits:
  - Public listing: co-sell eligibility depends on cloud partner rules; credits sometimes apply but tracking can be less direct.
  - Private Offer: typically cleaner for co-sell attribution because the seller-managed offer maps to the partner/rep.

- Timing and lead time:
  - Marketplace public: fastest for customers who accept marketplace invoices (days).
  - Private Offer: needs seller-side setup and often a private offer PO flow (1–2 weeks typical, can be faster with a templated PO).

Recommendation for RetailX pilot (based on your constraints):
1) Private Offer route — because you require seller bill-to and single SKU on PO.
2) We will propose a customer-specific SKU and provide an invoice template that aligns with your AP system.
3) If you want marketplace listing later for broader teams, we can pursue a dual approach: private offer for the pilot, public listing for self-serve after contract/usage thresholds.

Quick internal align: agree with private offer recommendation for the pilot. A few operational notes to share back to Rajiv:

- For AWS Private Offers we can request seller-billed invoicing and create a single offer SKU tied to RetailX. Typical lead time: 3–7 business days after PO receipt if finance has template.
- For Azure (Marketplace private/offline offer) the seller-of-record flow is similar but requires publishing an offer and a private link; expect 5–10 business days for initial setup if legal or trading terms are needed.
- GCP: Private pricing via reseller or partner works, but billing flows vary; confirm whether RetailX needs cloud-native credits — if so, co-sell attribution will need to be captured in the PO metadata.
